gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Birdfy feeders only charge, including from their solar panels, when the air is between 32°F and 104°F (0–40°C), or that their cameras are rated to work only down to 14°F (-10°C). Below freezing the 'solar, never recharge' plan stops, and on the coldest days the camera is outside its rated range. Birdbuddy rates its Home and Nook down to -5°F, but tells owners to charge the camera indoors at room temperature.
standout_why: I opened Reviewed (cited), Feeder Field, Digital Camera World and BirdFeederLab's Bird Buddy vs Birdfy page. WIRED, the other cited page, blocked my fetch, so I didn't check it. Reviewed lists IP ratings, battery mAh and solar wattage, and says 'Solar charging works best in yards with consistent sunlight', but gives no temperature limits at all. Feeder Field lists operating ranges (Birdfy 14–113°F, Bird Buddy -5–120°F) and the general line 'lithium batteries hold less charge in the cold', but no charging floor. Digital Camera World and BirdFeederLab say nothing about temperature. None of them says solar charging stops below 32°F. ChatGPT's own answer sells solar as 'Reduces manual battery charging' with no cold-weather caveat.
decides: In a yard that freezes in winter, solar can't keep any of these feeders charged through the cold months. Birdfy's own troubleshooting says charging works only at 32–104°F. Birdbuddy says to warm the camera to room temperature and charge it indoors. That makes battery size and the low-temperature rating matter more than solar wattage. Birdfy Metal 2 4K and Feeder 2 Pro are rated only down to 14°F, while Birdbuddy Home and Nook are rated to -5°F. In places that regularly drop below 14°F, Birdbuddy is the only maker of these candidates that rates its camera for that cold. In milder climates the Birdfy 9,000 mAh models still lead, because their larger battery lasts longer between indoor charges. Separate from my angle: Reviewed says the Feeder 2 Pro's AI needs a subscription after a 7-day trial ($79.99/yr), which conflicts with our page's 'Free for life'. Recheck that before publishing.

findings.label: Charging temperature range (solar or charger)
findings.value: 32°F to 104°F (0–40°C) ambient; outside it 'the camera may not charge properly'
findings.source_title: Birdfy Support – FAQ Troubleshooting (Charging, Q4: solar panel not charging)
findings.note: Verbatim: 'Make sure the ambient temperature while charging with the solar panel is between 0℃ and 40℃ (32℉ and 104℉).' The same FAQ says 'all Birdfy products are compatible with solar panels' and doesn't limit the range to particular models.

findings.label: Solar panel's job
findings.value: Keeps a full battery topped up; does not recharge a fully drained one
findings.source_title: Birdfy Hum Feeder SE – Charging Guidance
findings.note: Verbatim: 'The solar panel is designed to maintain a full battery, not to recharge a completely drained one.' This page is for the Hum Feeder SE. I'm treating it as Birdfy's general solar design, not confirmed for the seed feeders.
